verses.1:1: Now it came to pass after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, that the LORD spoke to Joshua the son of Nun, the attendant of Moses, saying,
verses.1:2: "My servant Moses is dead. Therefore arise now, cross over this Jordan—you and all this people—into the land that I am giving to them, to the children of Israel.
verses.1:3: Every place upon which the sole of your foot shall tread I have given to you, just as I spoke to Moses.
verses.1:4: From the wilderness and this Lebanon, even as far as the great river, the river Euphrates—all the land of the Hittites—and to the Great Sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your territory.
verses.1:5: No man shall stand before you all the days of your life; just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you, nor will I forsake you.
verses.1:6: Be strong and courageous, for you shall cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.
verses.1:7: Only be strong and exceedingly courageous, taking care to do according to all the law which Moses My servant commanded you; do not turn aside from it to the right hand or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.
verses.1:8: This Book of the Law shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your ways prosperous, and then you shall act wisely.
verses.1:9: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous! Do not tremble and do not be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
verses.1:10: Then Joshua commanded the officers of the people, saying,
verses.1:11: "Pass through the midst of the camp and command the people, saying, 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for within three days you are crossing over this Jordan to go in to possess the land which the LORD your God is giving you to possess it.'"
verses.1:12: And to the Reubenites, to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua spoke, saying,
verses.1:13: "Remember the word which Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, saying, 'The LORD your God is giving you rest and has given you this land.'
verses.1:14: Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock shall dwell in the land which Moses gave you beyond the Jordan; but you shall cross over armed before your brethren, all the mighty men of valor, and help them,
verses.1:15: until the LORD gives rest to your brethren as to you, and they also possess the land which the LORD your God is giving them. Then you shall return to the land of your possession and possess it, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun."
verses.1:16: So they answered Joshua, saying, "All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
verses.1:17: According to all that we heeded Moses, so we will heed you; only may the LORD your God be with you, just as He was with Moses.
verses.1:18: Every man who rebels against your command and does not heed your words in all that you command him shall be put to death; only be strong and courageous."
verses.2:1: Now Joshua the son of Nun sent out two men from Shittim as spies secretly, saying, "Go, view the land and Jericho." So they went and came to the house of a harlot whose name was Rahab, and lodged there.
verses.2:2: And it was told to the king of Jericho, saying, "Behold, men from the children of Israel have come here tonight to search out the land."
verses.2:3: So the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who have come to you, who have entered your house, for they have come to search out all the land."
verses.2:4: Then the woman took the two men and hid them. And she said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
verses.2:5: And it happened as the gate was about to be shut, in the darkness, that the men went out. I do not know where the men went; pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them."
verses.2:6: Now she had brought them up to the roof and concealed them under the stalks of flax which she had laid in order upon the roof.
verses.2:7: So the men pursued after them along the road to the Jordan as far as the fords; and they shut the gate as soon as those who pursued them had gone out.
verses.2:8: Now before they lay down, she came up to them on the roof,
verses.2:9: and said to the men, "I know that the LORD has given you the land, that the terror of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land have melted away because of you.
verses.2:10: For we have heard how the LORD dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed.
verses.2:11: And as soon as we heard, our hearts melted, and no spirit remained any longer in any man because of you; for the LORD your God, He is God in heaven above and on earth beneath.
verses.2:12: Now therefore, please swear to me by the LORD, since I have shown lovingkindness to you, that you also will show lovingkindness to my father's house, and give me a true token,
verses.2:13: and keep alive my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and all that belongs to them, and deliver our lives from death."
verses.2:14: So the men answered her, "Our lives for yours, even to death, if you do not report this business of ours! And it shall be, when the LORD gives us the land, that we will deal with you in lovingkindness and truth."
verses.2:15: Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was on the side of the city wall, and she dwelt on the wall.
verses.2:16: And she said to them, "Go to the hill country, lest the pursuers encounter you; and hide yourselves there three days until the pursuers have returned, and afterward you may go on your way."
verses.2:17: Then the men said to her, "We shall be guiltless of this oath of yours which you have made us swear:
verses.2:18: Behold, when we come into the land, you shall bind this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and you shall gather your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father's household to yourself into the house.
verses.2:19: And it shall be that whoever goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood shall be on his own head, and we shall be guiltless; and whoever is with you in the house, his blood shall be on our head if a hand is laid upon him.
verses.2:20: And if you report this business of ours, then we shall be free from your oath which you have made us swear."
verses.2:21: And she said, "According to your words, so let it be." Then she sent them away, and they departed; and she bound the scarlet cord in the window.
verses.2:22: So they departed and came to the hill country, and remained there three days until the pursuers returned. And the pursuers sought them all along the road, but did not find them.
verses.2:23: Then the two men returned, came down from the hill country, crossed over, and came to Joshua the son of Nun, and recounted to him all that had befallen them.
verses.2:24: And they said to Joshua, "Truly the LORD has delivered all the land into our hand; and indeed, all the inhabitants of the land have melted away before us."
verses.3:1: Then Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel, and lodged there before they crossed over.
verses.3:2: And it came to pass at the end of three days that the officers went through the midst of the camp,
verses.3:3: and they commanded the people, saying, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, and the priests, the Levites, bearing it, then you shall set out from your place and follow after it.
verses.3:4: Yet there shall be a distance between you and it of about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way by which you must go, for you have not passed this way before."
verses.3:5: And Joshua said to the people, "Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wondrous things in your midst."
verses.3:6: Then Joshua spoke to the priests, saying, "Take up the ark of the covenant and pass over before the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went before the people.
verses.3:7: And the LORD said to Joshua, "This day I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so that they may know that, just as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.
verses.3:8: And you shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, saying, 'When you come to the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you shall stand still in the Jordan.'"
verses.3:9: So Joshua said to the children of Israel, "Draw near here, and hear the words of the LORD your God."
verses.3:10: And Joshua said, "By this you shall know that the living God is in your midst, and that He will surely dispossess from before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites:
verses.3:11: Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing over before you into the Jordan.
verses.3:12: Now therefore, take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.
verses.3:13: And it shall come to pass, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, shall rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan shall be cut off—the waters that come down from above—and they shall stand as a single heap."
verses.3:14: So it came to pass, when the people set out from their tents to cross over the Jordan, with the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people,
verses.3:15: and as those who bore the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bore the ark were dipped in the edge of the water—for the Jordan overflows all its banks during all the days of harvest—
verses.3:16: that the waters which came down from above stood still and rose up in a single heap very far away, from Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and the waters going down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, failed and were cut off. And the people crossed over opposite Jericho.
verses.3:17: Then the priests who bore the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan; and all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the nation had completely crossed over the Jordan.
verses.4:1: And it came to pass, when all the nation had finished crossing over the Jordan, that the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
verses.4:2: "Take for yourselves twelve men from the people, one man from every tribe,
verses.4:3: and command them, saying, 'Take up for yourselves from here, out of the midst of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones; and carry them over with you, and lay them down in the lodging place where you will lodge tonight.'"
verses.4:4: Then Joshua summoned the twelve men whom he had appointed from the children of Israel, one man from every tribe.
verses.4:5: And Joshua said to them, "Cross over before the ark of the LORD your God into the midst of the Jordan, and each of you lift up one stone upon his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel,
verses.4:6: so that this may be a sign in your midst. When your children ask in time to come, saying, 'What do these stones mean to you?'
verses.4:7: then you shall answer them, 'The waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD; when it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off.' And these stones shall be for a memorial to the children of Israel forever."
verses.4:8: And the children of Israel did so, just as Joshua commanded, and took up twelve stones from the midst of the Jordan, as the LORD had spoken to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel; and they carried them over with them to the lodging place and laid them down there.
verses.4:9: Joshua also set up twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood; and they are there to this day.
verses.4:10: Now the priests who bore the ark remained standing in the midst of the Jordan until everything was finished that the LORD had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua; and the people hurried and crossed over.
verses.4:11: And it came to pass, when all the people had finished crossing over, that the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed over in the presence of the people.
verses.4:12: And the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed before the children of Israel, as Moses had spoken to them.
verses.4:13: About forty thousand men equipped for war crossed over before the LORD to battle, onto the plains of Jericho.
verses.4:14: On that day the LORD exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they revered him, just as they had revered Moses, all the days of his life.
verses.4:15: Then the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
verses.4:16: "Command the priests who bear the ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
verses.4:17: Joshua therefore commanded the priests, saying, "Come up out of the Jordan."
verses.4:18: And it came to pass, when the priests who bore the ark of the covenant of the LORD had come up from the midst of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted onto the dry ground, that the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and overflowed all its banks as before.
verses.4:19: Now the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho.
verses.4:20: And those twelve stones, which they had taken out of the Jordan, Joshua set up at Gilgal.
verses.4:21: Then he spoke to the children of Israel, saying, "When your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, 'What are these stones?'
verses.4:22: then you shall make it known to your children, saying, 'Israel crossed over this Jordan on dry land.'
verses.4:23: For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea, which He dried up before us until we had crossed over,
verses.4:24: so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty, and that you may fear the LORD your God forever."
verses.5:1: And it came to pass, when all the kings of the Amorites who were on the west side of the Jordan, and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea, heard that the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan from before the children of Israel until they had crossed over, that their heart melted, and there was no longer any spirit in them because of the children of Israel.
verses.5:2: At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make for yourself flint knives, and circumcise the children of Israel again the second time."
verses.5:3: So Joshua made flint knives for himself and circumcised the children of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.
verses.5:4: And this is the reason why Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt who were males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness along the way after they came out of Egypt.
verses.5:5: For all the people who came out had been circumcised, yet all the people who were born in the wilderness along the way after they came out of Egypt had not been circumcised.
verses.5:6: For the children of Israel walked forty years in the wilderness, until all the nation—the men of war who came out of Egypt—had perished, because they did not obey the voice of the LORD, to whom the LORD swore that He would not let them see the land which the LORD had sworn to their fathers to give to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.5:7: Then Joshua circumcised their sons whom He had raised up in their place; for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised along the way.
verses.5:8: And it came to pass, when all the nation had finished being circumcised, that they remained in their places in the camp until they were healed.
verses.5:9: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "This day I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." Therefore the name of that place has been called Gilgal to this day.
verses.5:10: Now the children of Israel encamped at Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening on the plains of Jericho.
verses.5:11: And on the day after the Passover they ate of the produce of the land, unleavened bread and parched grain, on that very day.
verses.5:12: Then the manna ceased on the day after they had eaten of the produce of the land; and the children of Israel no longer had manna, but they ate of the yield of the land of Canaan during that year.
verses.5:13: And it came to pass, when Joshua was by Jericho, that he lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, a man stood opposite him with his sword drawn in his hand. And Joshua went to him and said to him, "Are you for us, or for our adversaries?"
verses.5:14: And he said, "No; rather, as commander of the host of the LORD I have now come." And Joshua fell on his face to the earth and worshiped, and said to him, "What does my lord say to his servant?"
verses.5:15: Then the commander of the host of the LORD said to Joshua, "Take your sandal off your foot, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
verses.6:1: Now Jericho was tightly shut up because of the children of Israel; none went out, and none came in.
verses.6:2: And the LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have given Jericho into your hand, along with its king and the mighty men of valor.
verses.6:3: You shall march around the city, all you men of war, going around the city once. Thus you shall do for six days.
verses.6:5: And it shall come to pass, when they make a long blast with the ram's horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, that all the people shall shout with a great shout; then the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up, every man straight before him."
verses.6:6: Then Joshua the son of Nun summoned the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests bear seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the LORD."
verses.6:7: And he said to the people, "Go forward and march around the city, and let the armed men pass on before the ark of the LORD."
verses.6:8: And it came to pass, when Joshua had spoken to the people, that the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the LORD went forward and blew the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed behind them.
verses.6:9: The armed men marched before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard came after the ark, while the trumpets were blown continually.
verses.6:10: Now Joshua had commanded the people, saying, "You shall not shout nor let your voice be heard, nor shall any word go forth from your mouth, until the day I say to you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout."
verses.6:11: So he caused the ark of the LORD to go around the city, encircling it once; then they came into the camp and lodged in the camp.
verses.6:12: And Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.
verses.6:13: And the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of the LORD marched on continually and blew the trumpets; the armed men marched before them, and the rear guard came after the ark of the LORD, while the trumpets were blown continually.
verses.6:14: And on the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. Thus they did for six days.
verses.6:15: And it came to pass on the seventh day that they rose early at the dawning of the day and marched around the city in the same manner seven times; only on that day did they march around the city seven times.
verses.6:16: And at the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout, for the LORD has given you the city!
verses.6:17: And the city shall be devoted to destruction, it and all that is in it, to the LORD; only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers whom we sent.
verses.6:18: And as for you, keep yourselves from the things devoted to destruction, lest you bring yourselves under the ban when you take of the devoted things, and make the camp of Israel devoted to destruction, and bring trouble upon it.
verses.6:19: But all the silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD; they shall go into the treasury of the LORD."
verses.6:20: So the people shouted, and the trumpets were blown. And it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, that the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat. Then the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they captured the city.
verses.6:21: And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
verses.6:22: But to the two men who had spied out the land Joshua said, "Go into the house of the harlot, and bring out from there the woman and all that belongs to her, just as you swore to her."
verses.6:23: So the young men who had spied went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that belonged to her; they also brought out all her kindred and placed them outside the camp of Israel.
verses.6:24: And they burned the city with fire, and all that was in it; only the silver and the gold, and the vessels of bronze and iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.
verses.6:25: But Joshua spared Rahab the harlot, her father's household, and all that belonged to her; and she dwells in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
verses.6:26: Then Joshua charged them with an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed be the man before the LORD who rises up and builds this city, Jericho; at the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest he shall set up its gates."
verses.6:27: So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame was throughout all the land.
verses.7:1: Now the children of Israel acted unfaithfully in a trespass concerning the devoted things, for Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the devoted things; and the anger of the LORD burned against the children of Israel.
verses.7:2: And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth Aven, on the east side of Bethel, and spoke to them, saying, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.
verses.7:3: And they returned to Joshua and said to him, "Do not let all the people go up, but let about two thousand or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not weary all the people there, for they are few."
verses.7:4: So about three thousand men went up there from the people, and they fled before the men of Ai.
verses.7:5: And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six men of them, and pursued them from before the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them on the descent. Therefore the heart of the people melted and became like water.
verses.7:6: Then Joshua tore his garments and fell to the earth on his face before the ark of the LORD until evening, both he and the elders of Israel; and they cast dust upon their heads.
verses.7:7: And Joshua said, "Alas, Lord GOD, why have You brought this people over the Jordan at all—to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? Oh, that we had been content and dwelt on the other side of the Jordan!
verses.7:8: O Lord, what shall I say after Israel has turned their backs before their enemies?
verses.7:9: For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and surround us, and cut off our name from the earth. Then what will You do for Your great name?"
verses.7:10: So the LORD said to Joshua, "Arise! Why is it that you have fallen upon your face?
verses.7:11: Israel has sinned, and they have also transgressed My covenant which I commanded them. For they have even taken of the devoted things, and have both stolen and dealt deceitfully; and they have also put them among their own belongings.
verses.7:12: Therefore the children of Israel cannot stand before their enemies, but turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with you, unless you destroy the devoted things from your midst.
verses.7:13: Rise up, sanctify the people, and say, 'Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says the LORD God of Israel: There is a devoted thing in your midst, O Israel; you cannot stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from your midst.
verses.7:14: In the morning therefore you shall be brought near according to your tribes. And it shall be that the tribe which the LORD takes shall come near by families; and the family which the LORD takes shall come near by households; and the household which the LORD takes shall come near man by man.
verses.7:15: Then it shall be that he who is taken with the devoted thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed the covenant of the LORD, and because he has committed a disgraceful act in Israel.'"
verses.7:16: So Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
verses.7:17: He brought near the family of Judah, and he took the family of the Zerahites; and he brought near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
verses.7:18: Then he brought near his household man by man, and Achan the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
verses.7:19: Now Joshua said to Achan, "My son, I implore you, give glory to the LORD God of Israel, and make confession to Him, and tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me."
verses.7:20: And Achan answered Joshua and said, "Indeed, I have sinned against the LORD God of Israel, and this is what I have done:
verses.7:21: When I saw among the spoils a fine mantle of Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold fifty shekels in weight, then I coveted them and took them. And behold, they are hidden in the earth in the midst of my tent, with the silver beneath it."
verses.7:22: So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and behold, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver beneath it.
verses.7:23: And they took them from the midst of the tent, brought them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel, and laid them out before the LORD.
verses.7:24: Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, the silver, the mantle, the bar of gold, his sons, his daughters, his ox, his donkey, his flock, his tent, and all that he had, and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
verses.7:25: And Joshua said, "Why have you troubled us? The LORD will trouble you this day." So all Israel stoned him with stones; and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
verses.7:26: Then they raised over him a great heap of stones, still there to this day. So the LORD turned from the fierceness of His anger. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.
verses.8:1: Now the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid, nor be dismayed; take all the people of war with you, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
verses.8:2: And you shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. Only its spoil and its livestock you shall take as plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city behind it."
verses.8:3: So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up against Ai; and Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty men of valor and sent them out by night.
verses.8:4: And he commanded them, saying, "Behold, you shall lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Do not go very far from the city, but all of you be ready.
verses.8:5: Then I and all the people who are with me will draw near to the city; and it shall come to pass, when they come out against us as at the first, that we will flee before them.
verses.8:6: For they will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are fleeing before us as at the first!' Therefore we will flee before them.
verses.8:7: Then you shall rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.
verses.8:8: And it shall be, when you have taken the city, that you shall set the city on fire. According to the word of the LORD you shall do. Behold, I have commanded you."
verses.8:9: Joshua therefore sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and waited between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai; but Joshua lodged that night among the people.
verses.8:10: Then Joshua rose up early in the morning and mustered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.
verses.8:11: And all the people of war who were with him went up and drew near; and they came before the city and encamped on the north side of Ai, with a valley between him and Ai.
verses.8:12: So he took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city. Thus the people stationed all the camp that was on the north of the city, and its rear guard on the west of the city; and Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley.
verses.8:14: Now it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that the men of the city hurried and rose early and went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at an appointed place before the Arabah. Yet he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.
verses.8:15: And Joshua and all Israel pretended to be beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness.
verses.8:16: So all the people who were in Ai were summoned to pursue after them; and they pursued after Joshua and were drawn away from the city.
verses.8:17: And not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. So they left the city open and pursued after Israel.
verses.8:18: Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." And Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.
verses.8:19: So the ambush arose quickly from its place, and they ran as soon as he stretched out his hand; and they entered the city and captured it, and hurried to set the city on fire.
verses.8:20: And when the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and behold, the smoke of the city ascended to heaven. So they had no power to flee this way or that way, and the people who had fled to the wilderness turned back upon the pursuers.
verses.8:21: Now when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city ascended, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
verses.8:22: Then the others came out from the city against them, so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side and some on that side. And they struck them down, so that they left none of them remaining or escaping.
verses.8:23: But the king of Ai they captured alive, and brought him to Joshua.
verses.8:24: And it came to pass, when Israel had made an end of slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they pursued them, and when they had all fallen by the edge of the sword until they were consumed, that all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
verses.8:25: So it was that all who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand—all the people of Ai.
verses.8:27: Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel took as plunder for themselves, according to the word of the LORD which He had commanded Joshua.
verses.8:28: So Joshua burned Ai and made it a heap forever, a desolation to this day.
verses.8:29: And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until evening. And as the sun went down, Joshua commanded, and they took down his corpse from the tree, cast it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised over it a great heap of stones, to this day.
verses.9:1: And it came to pass, when all the kings who were beyond the Jordan, in the hill country and in the lowland and along all the shore of the Great Sea opposite Lebanon—the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—heard of these things,
verses.9:2: then Joshua built an altar to the LORD God of Israel on Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: an altar of whole stones, upon which no one had wielded any iron. And they offered upon it burnt offerings to the LORD, and sacrificed peace offerings. And there, on the stones, he wrote a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written in the presence of the children of Israel. And all Israel, with their elders and officers and judges, stood on either side of the ark before the Levitical priests who bore the ark of the covenant of the LORD, the sojourner as well as the native-born—half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal—as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded at the first, that they should bless the people of Israel. And afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the Book of the Law. There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded which Joshua did not read before all the assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones, and the sojourners who walked among them. And they gathered themselves together with one accord to fight against Joshua and against Israel.
verses.9:3: Now the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai.
verses.9:4: And they also acted craftily, and went and posed as envoys; and they took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and old wineskins, torn and bound up,
verses.9:5: and worn-out and patched sandals on their feet, and worn-out garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and crumbly.
verses.9:6: And they went to Joshua, to the camp at Gilgal, and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a far country; now therefore, make a covenant with us."
verses.9:7: And the men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Perhaps you dwell in our midst; how then shall we make a covenant with you?"
verses.9:8: And they said to Joshua, "We are your servants." And Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and from where do you come?"
verses.9:9: So they said to him, "From a very far country your servants have come, because of the name of the LORD your God; for we have heard of His fame, and all that He did in Egypt,
verses.9:10: and all that He did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan—to Sihon king of Heshbon, and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.
verses.9:11: Therefore our elders and all the inhabitants of our land spoke to us, saying, 'Take provisions in your hand for the journey, and go to meet them, and say to them, "We are your servants; now therefore, make a covenant with us."'
verses.9:12: This bread of ours we took hot for our provision from our houses on the day we departed to come to you; but now, behold, it is dry and has become crumbly.
verses.9:13: And these wineskins which we filled were new, and behold, they are torn; and these garments of ours and our sandals have become worn out because of the very long journey."
verses.9:14: Then the men took some of their provisions, and did not inquire at the mouth of the LORD.
verses.9:15: So Joshua made peace with them, and made a covenant with them to let them live; and the rulers of the congregation swore to them.
verses.9:16: And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a covenant with them, that they heard that they were near to them and dwelt in their midst.
verses.9:17: Then the children of Israel journeyed and came to their cities on the third day. Now their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
verses.9:18: And the children of Israel did not strike them, because the rulers of the congregation had sworn to them by the LORD God of Israel. And all the congregation murmured against the rulers.
verses.9:19: Then all the rulers said to all the congregation, "We have sworn to them by the LORD God of Israel; now therefore, we may not touch them.
verses.9:20: This we will do to them: we will let them live, lest wrath come upon us because of the oath which we swore to them."
verses.9:21: And the rulers said to them, "Let them live." So they became hewers of wood and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the rulers had spoken to them.
verses.9:22: Then Joshua summoned them and spoke to them, saying, "Why have you deceived us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when you dwell in our midst?
verses.9:23: Now therefore you are cursed, and there shall never fail to be bondservants from among you—both hewers of wood and drawers of water for the house of my God."
verses.9:24: And they answered Joshua and said, "Because it was certainly told to your servants how the LORD your God commanded His servant Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you; therefore we feared greatly for our lives because of you, and have done this thing.
verses.9:25: And now, behold, we are in your hand; do as it seems good and right in your sight to do to us."
verses.9:26: So he did so to them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, so that they did not slay them.
verses.9:27: And that day Joshua made them hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to this very day, in the place which He would choose.
verses.10:1: Now it came to pass when Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had captured Ai and had utterly destroyed it—as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he had done to Ai and its king—and how the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,
verses.10:2: that they feared exceedingly, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.
verses.10:3: Therefore Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish, and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,
verses.10:4: "Come up to me and help me, that we may strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel."
verses.10:5: Therefore the five kings of the Amorites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered themselves together and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped before Gibeon and made war against it.
verses.10:6: And the men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not withdraw your hands from your servants; come up to us quickly, save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country have gathered together against us."
verses.10:7: So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.
verses.10:8: And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have delivered them into your hand; not a man of them shall stand before you."
verses.10:9: Joshua therefore came upon them suddenly, having marched up all night from Gilgal.
verses.10:10: So the LORD routed them before Israel, and struck them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and pursued them along the road of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
verses.10:11: And it came to pass, as they fled from before Israel and were on the descent of Beth-horon, that the LORD cast down large stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel slew with the sword.
verses.10:12: Then Joshua spoke to the LORD on the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel, "Sun, stand still over Gibeon; and Moon, in the Valley of Aijalon!"
verses.10:13: So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance upon its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? So the sun stood in the midst of heaven, and did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.
verses.10:14: And there has been no day like that, before it or after it, that the LORD heeded the voice of a man; for the LORD fought for Israel.
verses.10:16: But these five kings had fled and hidden themselves in the cave at Makkedah.
verses.10:17: And it was told to Joshua, saying, "The five kings have been found hidden in the cave at Makkedah."
verses.10:18: And Joshua said, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to guard them.
verses.10:19: And do not stay there yourselves, but pursue after your enemies, and strike down their rear guard. Do not allow them to enter their cities, for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand."
verses.10:20: And it came to pass, when Joshua and the children of Israel had finished striking them with a very great slaughter until they were consumed, that the survivors who remained of them entered the fortified cities.
verses.10:21: And all the people returned to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace. No one moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.
verses.10:22: Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings to me from the cave."
verses.10:23: And they did so, and brought out those five kings to him from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
verses.10:24: And it came to pass, when they brought out those kings to Joshua, that Joshua called for all the men of Israel, and said to the captains of the men of war who went with him, "Come near, put your feet on the necks of these kings." And they drew near and put their feet on their necks.
verses.10:25: Then Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid, nor be dismayed; be strong and of good courage, for thus the LORD will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."
verses.10:26: And afterward Joshua struck them and put them to death, and hanged them on five trees; and they were hanging on the trees until evening.
verses.10:27: And it came to pass at the time of the going down of the sun that Joshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees, cast them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and placed large stones against the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.
verses.10:28: On that day Joshua captured Makkedah, and struck it and its king with the edge of the sword. He utterly destroyed them and every soul who was in it; he left no survivor. And he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
verses.10:29: Then Joshua passed from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah; and he fought against Libnah.
verses.10:30: And the LORD also delivered it and its king into the hand of Israel; and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every soul who was in it. He left no survivor in it, and did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
verses.10:31: Then Joshua passed from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish; and he encamped against it and fought against it.
verses.10:32: And the LORD delivered Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every soul who was in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.
verses.10:33: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua struck him and his people, until he had left him no survivor.
verses.10:34: From Lachish Joshua passed to Eglon, and all Israel with him; and they encamped against it and fought against it.
verses.10:35: And they captured it on that day and struck it with the edge of the sword; and every soul who was in it he utterly destroyed on that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.
verses.10:36: Then Joshua went up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron; and they fought against it.
verses.10:37: And they captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword—its king, all its towns, and every soul who was in it; he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon, and utterly destroyed it and every soul who was in it.
verses.10:38: Then Joshua turned back, and all Israel with him, to Debir; and he fought against it.
verses.10:39: And he captured it and its king and all its towns; and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroyed every soul who was in it. He left no survivor; as he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.
verses.10:40: So Joshua struck all the land: the hill country, the Negev, the lowland, and the slopes, and all their kings. He left no survivor, but utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the LORD God of Israel had commanded.
verses.10:41: And Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea even as far as Gaza, and all the land of Goshen, even as far as Gibeon.
verses.10:42: All these kings and their land Joshua captured at one time, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
verses.11:1: Now it came to pass, when Jabin king of Hazor heard this, that he sent to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
verses.11:2: and to the kings who were in the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west,
verses.11:3: to the Canaanites on the east and on the west, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites below Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
verses.11:4: So they went out, they and all their armies with them, a great multitude, as numerous as the sand that is upon the seashore, with very many horses and chariots.
verses.11:5: Then all these kings assembled together, and they came and encamped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
verses.11:6: And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid before them, for tomorrow at this very time I will give them all up slain before Israel; their horses you shall hamstring, and their chariots you shall burn with fire."
verses.11:7: So Joshua and all the men of war with him came against them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and they fell upon them.
verses.11:8: And the LORD delivered them into the hand of Israel; they struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, to Misrephoth Maim, and to the Valley of Mizpeh eastward; and they struck them down until they left them no survivor.
verses.11:9: So Joshua did to them just as the LORD had spoken to him: their horses he hamstrung, and their chariots he burned with fire.
verses.11:10: Then Joshua turned back at that time and captured Hazor, and its king he struck down with the sword; for Hazor formerly was the head of all those kingdoms.
verses.11:11: And they struck every soul who was in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them; nothing that breathed remained, and he burned Hazor with fire.
verses.11:12: And all the cities of those kings, and all their kings, Joshua captured, and he struck them with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
verses.11:13: Yet as for all the cities that stood on their mounds, Israel did not burn them, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.
verses.11:14: And all the spoil of those cities, along with the livestock, the children of Israel took as plunder for themselves; only every person they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them, and they left nothing that breathed.
verses.11:15: Just as the LORD had commanded Moses His servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did; he did not omit a single thing of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.11:16: Thus Joshua took all this land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel and its lowland,
verses.11:17: from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, even as far as Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon; and all their kings he captured, struck down, and put to death.
verses.11:18: For many days Joshua made war with all those kings.
verses.11:19: There was not a city that made peace with the children of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon; all the others they took in battle.
verses.11:20: For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts to meet Israel in battle, that they might be utterly destroyed and receive no mercy, but be annihilated, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.11:21: And Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel; Joshua utterly destroyed them along with their cities.
verses.11:22: None of the Anakim were left in the land of the children of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod did some remain.
verses.11:23: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD had spoken to Moses; and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. Then the land had rest from war.
verses.12:1: Now these are the kings of the land whom the children of Israel struck down, and whose land they took in possession beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the Brook Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:
verses.12:2: Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer, which is on the bank of the Brook Arnon, and from the middle of the valley, and over half of Gilead, as far as the Brook Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon;
verses.12:3: and over the Arabah to the Sea of Chinneroth eastward, and to the Sea of the Arabah—the Salt Sea—eastward, by the way of Beth Jeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.
verses.12:4: And the territory of Og king of Bashan, who was of the remnant of the Rephaim, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
verses.12:5: and ruled over Mount Hermon, over Salecah, and over all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maachathites, and over half of Gilead to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
verses.12:6: Moses the servant of the LORD and the children of Israel struck them down; and Moses the servant of the LORD gave it as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.12:7: And these are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck down beyond the Jordan on the west, from Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon even to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir; and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,
verses.12:8: in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Arabah, in the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the Negev—the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites:
verses.12:9: the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
verses.12:10: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
verses.12:11: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
verses.12:12: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
verses.12:13: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
verses.12:14: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
verses.12:15: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
verses.12:16: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
verses.12:17: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
verses.12:18: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
verses.12:19: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
verses.12:20: the king of Shimron Meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
verses.12:21: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
verses.12:22: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
verses.12:23: the king of Dor in the height of Dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
verses.12:24: the king of Tirzah, one; in all, thirty-one kings.
verses.13:1: Now Joshua was old and advanced in years. And the LORD said to him, "You are old and advanced in years, and very much of the land still remains to be possessed.
verses.13:2: This is the land that yet remains: all the regions of the Philistines and all those of the Geshurites,
verses.13:3: from the Shihor, which is east of Egypt, even as far as the border of Ekron northward, which is reckoned as Canaanite—the five lords of the Philistines: the Gazites, the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites, and also the Avvim.
verses.13:4: In the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
verses.13:5: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the rising of the sun, from Baal Gad beneath Mount Hermon as far as the entrance to Hamath;
verses.13:6: all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Misrephoth Maim, even all the Sidonians—I Myself will drive them out from before the children of Israel. Only allot it to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
verses.13:7: Now therefore, divide this land as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
verses.13:8: With the other half-tribe, the Reubenites and the Gadites received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan eastward, just as Moses the servant of the LORD gave them:
verses.13:9: from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the valley, and all the plain of Medeba as far as Dibon;
verses.13:10: all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the children of Ammon;
verses.13:11: and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
verses.13:12: all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei; he was left of the remnant of the Rephaim, for Moses had struck them down and dispossessed them.
verses.13:13: Nevertheless, the children of Israel did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites; so Geshur and Maacath dwell in the midst of Israel to this day.
verses.13:14: Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance; the offerings made by fire to the LORD God of Israel are his inheritance, as He spoke to him.
verses.13:15: And Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their families.
verses.13:16: And their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the valley, and all the plain by Medeba;
verses.13:17: Heshbon and all its cities that are in the plain: Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,
verses.13:19: Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar on the mountain of the valley,
verses.13:20: Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth Jeshimoth—
verses.13:21: all the cities of the plain and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down along with the leaders of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, who were princes of Sihon dwelling in the land.
verses.13:22: The children of Israel also slew Balaam the son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword among the rest of their slain.
verses.13:23: And the border of the children of Reuben was the Jordan and its bank. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their families, the cities and their villages.
verses.13:24: Moses also gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the children of Gad according to their families.
verses.13:25: Their territory was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon as far as Aroer, which is east of Rabbah,
verses.13:26: and from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;
verses.13:27: and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan and its bank as the border, as far as the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan eastward.
verses.13:28: This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and their villages.
verses.13:29: Moses also gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it belonged to the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.
verses.13:30: Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair that are in Bashan, sixty cities;
verses.13:31: and half of Gilead, with Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, belonged to the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, for half of the children of Machir according to their families.
verses.13:32: These are the inheritances that Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward.
verses.14:1: Now these are the inheritances that the children of Israel received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the children of Israel distributed to them.
verses.14:2: Their inheritance was by lot, as the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
verses.14:3: For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.
verses.14:4: For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; therefore they gave no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell in, with their pasturelands for their livestock and their possessions.
verses.14:5: Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did, and they divided the land.
verses.14:6: Then the children of Judah drew near to Joshua in Gilgal. And Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know the word which the LORD spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you at Kadesh Barnea.
verses.14:7: I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back word to him as it was in my heart.
verses.14:8: Yet my brethren who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, but I wholly followed the LORD my God.
verses.14:9: So Moses swore on that day, saying, 'Surely the land on which your foot has trodden shall be an inheritance for you and for your children forever, because you have wholly followed the LORD my God.'
verses.14:10: And now, behold, the LORD has kept me alive, as He spoke, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses while Israel walked in the wilderness; and now, behold, I am this day eighty-five years old.
verses.14:11: I am still as strong this day as on the day Moses sent me; just as my strength was then, so is my strength now for war, both for going out and for coming in.
verses.14:12: Now therefore, give me this hill country of which the LORD spoke on that day; for you yourself heard on that day that the Anakim were there, and great fortified cities. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I shall drive them out, as the LORD has spoken."
verses.14:13: Then Joshua blessed him, and gave Hebron to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance.
verses.14:14: Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he wholly followed the LORD God of Israel.
verses.14:15: Now the name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath Arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.
verses.15:1: Now the lot for the tribe of the children of Judah, according to their families, reached to the border of Edom, the Wilderness of Zin southward, at the utmost end of the south.
verses.15:2: And their southern border began at the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces southward.
verses.15:3: It went out to the south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, passed over to Zin, and went up on the south side of Kadesh Barnea; then it passed along to Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned around to Karka.
verses.15:4: And it passed over to Azmon and went out to the Brook of Egypt, and the ends of the border were at the sea. This shall be your southern border.
verses.15:5: And the eastern border was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. And the border on the northern side was from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.
verses.15:6: Then the border went up to Beth Hoglah and passed north of Beth Arabah; and the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.
verses.15:7: And the border went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and turned northward toward Gilgal, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, on the south side of the brook; then the border passed along to the waters of En Shemesh, and its ends were at En Rogel.
verses.15:8: Then the border went up by the Valley of the Son of Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite, which is Jerusalem; and the border went up to the top of the mountain that lies before the Valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the end of the Valley of Rephaim northward.
verses.15:9: And the border curved from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and went out to the cities of Mount Ephron; then the border curved to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim.
verses.15:10: Then the border turned around from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, passed along to the northern slope of Mount Jearim, which is Chesalon, went down to Beth Shemesh, and passed on to Timnah.
verses.15:11: And the border went out to the slope of Ekron northward; and the border curved to Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, and went out to Jabneel; and the ends of the border were at the sea.
verses.15:12: And the western border was the Great Sea and its coastline. This was the border of the children of Judah all around, according to their families.
verses.15:13: Now to Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the children of Judah, according to the command of the LORD to Joshua, namely, Kiriath Arba—Arba was the father of Anak—which is Hebron.
verses.15:14: And Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the offspring of Anak.
verses.15:15: Then he went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir. Now the name of Debir formerly was Kiriath Sepher.
verses.15:16: And Caleb said, "He who strikes Kiriath Sepher and captures it, to him I will give Achsah my daughter as a wife."
verses.15:17: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, captured it; and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.
verses.15:18: Now it came to pass, when she came, that she urged him to ask her father for a field. And she dismounted from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you wish?"
verses.15:19: And she said, "Give me a blessing; since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
verses.15:20: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.
verses.15:21: Now the cities at the farthest limits of the tribe of the children of Judah, toward the border of Edom in the Negev, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
verses.15:25: Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron, which is Hazor,
verses.15:32: Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon: all the cities were twenty-nine, with their villages.
verses.15:33: In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
verses.15:36: Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim: fourteen cities with their villages.
verses.15:41: Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah: sixteen cities with their villages.
verses.15:44: Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah: nine cities with their villages.
verses.15:45: Ekron, with its towns and its villages;
verses.15:46: from Ekron westward, all that lay beside Ashdod, with their villages;
verses.15:47: Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt and the Great Sea with its coastline.
verses.15:48: And in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
verses.15:49: Dannah, Kiriath Sannah, which is Debir,
verses.15:51: Goshen, Holon, and Giloh: eleven cities with their villages.
verses.15:54: Humtah, Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, and Zior: nine cities with their villages.
verses.15:57: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah: ten cities with their villages.
verses.15:59: Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon: six cities with their villages.
verses.15:60: Kiriath Baal, which is Kiriath Jearim, and Rabbah: two cities with their villages.
verses.15:61: In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
verses.15:62: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi: six cities with their villages.
verses.15:63: As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out; so the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem to this day.
verses.16:1: Then the allotment went out for the sons of Joseph from the Jordan of Jericho to the waters of Jericho eastward, through the wilderness ascending from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
verses.16:2: From Bethel it extended to Luz, and crossed over toward the territory of the Archites at Ataroth.
verses.16:3: Then it descended westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth Horon and on to Gezer, and its farthest limits reached to the sea.
verses.16:4: Thus the sons of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
verses.16:5: Now this was the boundary of the sons of Ephraim according to their clans: the border of their inheritance on the east ran from Ataroth Addar as far as Upper Beth Horon.
verses.16:6: And the boundary extended toward the sea, with Michmethath on the north; then the boundary curved eastward to Taanath Shiloh, and passed beyond it on the east of Janohah.
verses.16:7: From Janohah it descended to Ataroth and to Naarah, touched upon Jericho, and came out at the Jordan.
verses.16:8: From Tappuah the boundary proceeded westward to the Brook of Kanah, and its farthest limits reached to the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim according to their clans,
verses.16:9: together with the cities set apart for the sons of Ephraim within the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh—all those cities along with their surrounding villages.
verses.16:10: Yet they did not dispossess the Canaanites who dwelt in Gezer; therefore the Canaanites have dwelt in the midst of Ephraim even to this very day, and became subject to forced labor.
verses.17:1: There was also an allotment for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was the firstborn of Joseph: for Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh and father of Gilead, since he was a man of war, Gilead and Bashan belonged to him.
verses.17:2: And an allotment was made for the remaining sons of Manasseh according to their clans: for the sons of Abiezer, the sons of Helek, the sons of Asriel, the sons of Shechem, the sons of Hepher, and the sons of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to their clans.
verses.17:3: Now Zelophehad the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. And these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
verses.17:4: They came near before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the leaders, saying, "The LORD commanded Moses to grant us an inheritance in the midst of our brethren." Therefore, according to the word of the LORD, he granted them an inheritance in the midst of their father's brethren.
verses.17:5: Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, apart from the land of Gilead and Bashan, which lies beyond the Jordan,
verses.17:6: because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance in the midst of his sons; and the land of Gilead belonged to the remaining sons of Manasseh.
verses.17:7: Now the boundary of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, which faces Shechem; and the boundary proceeded southward toward the inhabitants of En Tappuah.
verses.17:8: The region of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, yet Tappuah itself on the border of Manasseh belonged to the sons of Ephraim.
verses.17:9: Then the boundary descended to the Brook of Kanah, on the south side of the brook—these cities belonged to Ephraim within the cities of Manasseh—while the boundary of Manasseh lay on the north side of the brook, and its farthest limits reached to the sea.
verses.17:10: The south side belonged to Ephraim and the north side to Manasseh, with the sea as its border; they joined Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
verses.17:11: Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also possessed Beth Shean and its dependent towns, Ibleam and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of En Dor and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its dependent towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its dependent towns—three elevated regions.
verses.17:12: Yet the sons of Manasseh were unable to take possession of these cities, for the Canaanites resolved to remain dwelling in that land.
verses.17:13: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel grew strong, that they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, yet did not completely dispossess them.
verses.17:14: Then the sons of Joseph spoke with Joshua, saying, "Why have you assigned to me only one lot and one portion as an inheritance, when I am a numerous people, since the LORD has blessed me so abundantly until now?"
verses.17:15: Joshua answered them, "If you are indeed a numerous people, go up for yourself into the forest and clear ground for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."
verses.17:16: And the sons of Joseph replied, "The hill country is not sufficient for us; moreover, all the Canaanites who dwell in the valley land possess chariots of iron—both those in Beth Shean and its dependent towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.17:17: Then Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph—to Ephraim and to Manasseh—saying, "You are a numerous people and possess great might; you shall not have merely one allotment.
verses.17:18: Rather, the hill country shall belong to you; though it is a forest, you shall clear it, and its farthest limits shall be yours. For you shall indeed dispossess the Canaanites, even though they have chariots of iron and even though they are mighty."
verses.18:1: Then the entire assembly of the children of Israel gathered together at Shiloh and erected the tent of meeting there; and the land was subdued before them.
verses.18:2: Yet among the children of Israel there remained seven tribes whose inheritance had not yet been apportioned.
verses.18:3: So Joshua said to the children of Israel, "How long will you slacken your hands from going in to take possession of the land which the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?
verses.18:4: Appoint for yourselves three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They shall arise, walk throughout the land, write a description of it in accordance with their inheritance, and return to me.
verses.18:5: They shall divide it into seven portions: Judah shall remain within its territory on the south, and the house of Joseph shall remain within their territory on the north.
verses.18:6: You shall record the land in seven portions and bring the description here to me, so that I may cast lots for you in this place before the LORD our God.
verses.18:7: For the Levites have no portion in your midst, because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance; and Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance beyond the Jordan toward the east, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."
verses.18:8: Then the men arose and departed; and Joshua charged those who were setting out to record the land, saying, "Go, walk throughout the land, write a description of it, and return to me; and here I will cast lots for you before the LORD at Shiloh."
verses.18:9: So the men went and traversed the land, and recorded it city by city in seven portions upon a scroll; then they returned to Joshua at the encampment in Shiloh.
verses.18:10: And Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD; and there Joshua apportioned the land to the children of Israel according to their divisions.
verses.18:11: Now the lot of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin came up according to their clans, and the territory of their allotment lay between the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph.
verses.18:12: On the northern side their boundary began from the Jordan; the boundary ascended to the slope of Jericho on the north, continued upward through the hill country westward, and its farthest limits reached to the wilderness of Beth Aven.
verses.18:13: From there the boundary crossed over to Luz, along the southern slope of Luz—that is, Bethel—and the boundary descended to Ataroth Addar, upon the mountain that lies south of Lower Beth Horon.
verses.18:14: Then the boundary turned and curved around on the western side southward, from the mountain that faces Beth Horon on the south, and its farthest limits reached to Kiriath Baal—that is, Kiriath Jearim—a city belonging to the sons of Judah. This formed the western side.
verses.18:15: The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim; the boundary extended westward and came out at the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
verses.18:16: Then the boundary descended to the foot of the mountain facing the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, which lies at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim; it descended through the Valley of Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite ridge, and went down to En Rogel.
verses.18:17: From there it turned northward, came out at En Shemesh, continued to Geliloth opposite the Ascent of Adummim, and descended to the Stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.
verses.18:18: It passed along to the slope facing the Arabah on the north and went down into the Arabah.
verses.18:19: Then the boundary crossed over to the northern slope of Beth Hoglah, and the farthest limits of the boundary reached to the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern mouth of the Jordan. This formed the southern boundary.
verses.18:20: And the Jordan formed its border on the eastern side. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin, bounded on every side according to their clans.
verses.18:21: Now the cities belonging to the tribe of the sons of Benjamin according to their clans were Jericho, Beth Hoglah, and Emek Keziz,
verses.18:24: Chephar Ammonah, Ophni, and Geba—twelve cities along with their surrounding villages;
verses.18:28: Zela, Haeleph, the Jebusite city, that is, Jerusalem, Gibeath, and Kiriath—fourteen cities along with their surrounding villages. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin according to their clans.
verses.19:1: The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families. And their inheritance was within the inheritance of the children of Judah.
verses.19:2: They had in their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah,
verses.19:5: Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, and Hazar Susah,
verses.19:6: Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen cities and their villages.
verses.19:7: Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four cities and their villages;
verses.19:8: and all the villages that were around these cities as far as Baalath Beer, Ramath of the South. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families.
verses.19:9: From the portion of the children of Judah came the inheritance of the children of Simeon, for the share of the children of Judah was too great for them; therefore the children of Simeon received their inheritance within their inheritance.
verses.19:10: The third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families, and the border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
verses.19:11: Their border went up westward to Maralah, touched Dabbasheth, and reached the brook that faces Jokneam.
verses.19:12: Then from Sarid it turned eastward toward the rising of the sun to the border of Chisloth Tabor, went out to Daberath, and went up to Japhia.
verses.19:13: From there it passed along eastward toward the sunrise to Gath Hepher, to Eth Kazin, and went out to Rimmon, curving toward Neah.
verses.19:14: Then the border went around it on the north to Hannathon, and its endpoints were the Valley of Jiphthah El.
verses.19:15: Also Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities and their villages.
verses.19:16: This was the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families, these cities and their villages.
verses.19:17: The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the children of Issachar according to their families.
verses.19:18: And their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
verses.19:21: Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
verses.19:22: And the border reached Tabor, Shahazimah, and Beth Shemesh; and the endpoints of their border were at the Jordan: sixteen cities and their villages.
verses.19:23: This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities and their villages.
verses.19:24: The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families.
verses.19:25: And their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
verses.19:26: Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal; it reached Carmel on the west, and Shihor Libnath.
verses.19:27: Then it turned toward the rising of the sun to Beth Dagon, and reached Zebulun and the Valley of Jiphthah El northward to Beth Emek and Neiel, and went out to Cabul on the left,
verses.19:28: and to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.
verses.19:29: Then the border turned to Ramah and as far as the fortified city of Tyre; then the border turned to Hosah, and its endpoints were at the sea from the region of Achzib.
verses.19:30: Also Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two cities and their villages.
verses.19:31: This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families, these cities and their villages.
verses.19:32: The sixth lot came out for the children of Naphtali, for the children of Naphtali according to their families.
verses.19:33: And their border ran from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, and Adami Nekeb, and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum; and its endpoints were at the Jordan.
verses.19:34: Then the border turned westward to Aznoth Tabor, and went out from there to Hukkok; it reached Zebulun on the south, and reached Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.
verses.19:35: And the fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
verses.19:38: Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh: nineteen cities and their villages.
