verses.19:39: This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities and their villages.
verses.19:40: The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families.
verses.19:41: And the territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,
verses.19:46: Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the territory opposite Joppa.
verses.19:47: This was the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, these cities and their villages.
verses.19:48: And the territory of the children of Dan went beyond them; so the children of Dan went up and fought against Leshem, captured it, and struck it with the edge of the sword. They possessed it and dwelt in it, and they called Leshem Dan, after the name of Dan their father.
verses.19:49: When they had finished dividing the land as an inheritance according to its borders, the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun in their midst.
verses.19:50: According to the command of the LORD they gave him the city for which he asked, Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city and dwelt in it.
verses.19:51: These are the inheritances which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers' houses of the tribes of the children of Israel distributed as an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before the LORD, at the doorway of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
verses.20:1: And the LORD spoke to Joshua, saying,
verses.20:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, saying, 'Appoint for yourselves the cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you through Moses,
verses.20:3: that the slayer who kills a person unintentionally, without knowledge, may flee there; and they shall be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood.'"
verses.20:7: So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba—that is, Hebron—in the hill country of Judah.
verses.20:8: And beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they appointed Bezer in the wilderness on the tableland, from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.
verses.20:9: These were the cities appointed for all the children of Israel and for the sojourner who dwells among them, that whoever kills a person unintentionally might flee there, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stood before the congregation.
verses.21:1: Then the heads of the fathers' households of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers' households of the tribes of the children of Israel.
verses.21:2: And they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "The LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities in which to dwell, together with their pasturelands for our livestock."
verses.21:3: So the children of Israel gave to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the command of the LORD, these cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:4: Now the lot came out for the families of the Kohathites. And the sons of Aaron the priest, who were of the Levites, received by lot thirteen cities from the tribe of Judah, from the tribe of the Simeonites, and from the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.21:5: And the remaining sons of Kohath received by lot ten cities from the families of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.21:6: And the sons of Gershon received by lot thirteen cities from the families of the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
verses.21:7: The sons of Merari according to their families received twelve cities from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun.
verses.21:8: Thus the children of Israel gave these cities with their pasturelands by lot to the Levites, as the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses.
verses.21:9: So they gave from the tribe of the children of Judah and from the tribe of the children of Simeon these cities which are designated by name.
verses.21:10: And they fell to the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, of the sons of Levi, for the first lot belonged to them.
verses.21:11: And they gave them Kiriath Arba, the father of Anak—which is Hebron—in the hill country of Judah, together with its pasturelands around it.
verses.21:12: But the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh as his possession.
verses.21:13: Thus to the sons of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Libnah with its pasturelands,
verses.21:14: and Jattir with its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
verses.21:15: and Holon with its pasturelands, and Debir with its pasturelands,
verses.21:16: and Ain with its pasturelands, and Juttah with its pasturelands, and Beth Shemesh with its pasturelands—nine cities from these two tribes;
verses.21:17: and from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasturelands, Geba with its pasturelands,
verses.21:18: Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands—four cities.
verses.21:19: All the cities of the sons of Aaron, the priests, were thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
verses.21:20: As for the families of the sons of Kohath, the Levites, the rest of the sons of Kohath, the cities of their lot were from the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.21:21: And they gave them Shechem with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Gezer with its pasturelands,
verses.21:22: and Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Beth Horon with its pasturelands—four cities;
verses.21:23: and from the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasturelands, Gibbethon with its pasturelands,
verses.21:24: Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath Rimmon with its pasturelands—four cities;
verses.21:25: and from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasturelands and Gath Rimmon with its pasturelands—two cities.
verses.21:26: All the cities with their pasturelands for the remaining families of the sons of Kohath were ten.
verses.21:27: And to the sons of Gershon, of the families of the Levites, they gave from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands—two cities;
verses.21:28: and from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
verses.21:29: Jarmuth with its pasturelands, and En Gannim with its pasturelands—four cities;
verses.21:30: and from the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
verses.21:31: Helkath with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands—four cities;
verses.21:32: and from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, Hammoth Dor with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands—three cities.
verses.21:33: All the cities of the Gershonites according to their families were thirteen cities with their pasturelands.
verses.21:34: And to the families of the sons of Merari, the rest of the Levites, they gave from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam with its pasturelands, Kartah with its pasturelands,
verses.21:35: Dimnah with its pasturelands, and Nahalal with its pasturelands—four cities;
verses.21:36: ⟦and from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasturelands, and Jahaz with its pasturelands,⟧
verses.21:37: ⟦Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands—four cities;⟧
verses.21:38: and from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, the city of refuge for the manslayer, and Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
verses.21:39: Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands—four cities in all.
verses.21:40: So all the cities for the sons of Merari according to their families, who remained of the families of the Levites, were by their lot twelve cities.
verses.21:41: All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty-eight cities with their pasturelands.
verses.21:42: Each of these cities had its pasturelands all around it; thus it was with every one of these cities.
verses.21:43: Thus the LORD gave Israel all the land that He had sworn to give to their fathers, and they possessed it and dwelt in it.
verses.21:44: And the LORD granted them rest on every side, according to all that He had sworn to their fathers. Not a man of all their enemies stood before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand.
verses.21:45: Not a single word failed of every good promise that the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel; everything came to pass.
verses.22:1: Then Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.22:2: And he said to them, "You have kept everything that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I have commanded you.
verses.22:3: You have not forsaken your brethren these many days, to this day, and you have kept the charge of the commandment of the LORD your God.
verses.22:4: And now the LORD your God has given rest to your brethren, as He spoke to them; therefore now turn and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan.
verses.22:5: Only take great care to observe the commandment and the law which Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to cleave to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul."
verses.22:6: So Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.
verses.22:7: Now to half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a portion in Bashan, and to its other half Joshua gave a portion among their brethren on the side of the Jordan westward. And indeed, when Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them.
verses.22:8: And he spoke to them, saying, "Return to your tents with great riches and with very much livestock, with silver, with gold, with bronze, with iron, and with very many garments. Divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren."
verses.22:9: So the children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh returned and departed from the children of Israel at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they had come to possess according to the command of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
verses.22:10: And when they came to the districts of the Jordan that are in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan, a great altar to behold.
verses.22:11: Now the children of Israel heard it said, "Behold, the children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar facing the land of Canaan, in the districts of the Jordan, on the side belonging to the children of Israel."
verses.22:12: And when the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh to go up against them in war.
verses.22:13: Then the children of Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest to the children of Reuben, to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead.
verses.22:14: And with him were ten chiefs, one chief from each father's house of all the tribes of Israel; each of them was the head of his father's house among the thousands of Israel.
verses.22:15: Then they came to the children of Reuben, to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, and they spoke with them, saying,
verses.22:16: "Thus says the entire congregation of the LORD: What is this treachery that you have committed against the God of Israel, turning away this day from following the LORD by building for yourselves an altar, to rebel this day against the LORD?
verses.22:17: Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves even to this day, although a plague came upon the congregation of the LORD,
verses.22:18: that you must turn away this day from following the LORD? And it shall come to pass that if you rebel today against the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
verses.22:19: Yet if the land of your possession is unclean, then cross over to the land of the possession of the LORD, where the tabernacle of the LORD dwells, and take possession among us; but do not rebel against the LORD, nor rebel against us, by building for yourselves an altar besides the altar of the LORD our God.
verses.22:20: Did not Achan the son of Zerah act treacherously regarding the devoted things, and wrath fell upon the whole congregation of Israel? And that one man did not perish alone in his iniquity."
verses.22:21: Then the children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the heads of the thousands of Israel:
verses.22:22: "The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD! He knows, and let Israel itself know: if it is in rebellion or in treachery against the LORD—do not save us this day—
verses.22:23: that we have built for ourselves an altar to turn from following the LORD, or if to offer upon it a burnt offering or grain offering, or if to offer upon it sacrifices of peace offerings, may the LORD Himself require it.
verses.22:24: Rather, we have indeed done this out of anxiety over this matter, saying: In time to come your children might speak to our children, saying, 'What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
verses.22:25: For the LORD has set the Jordan as a border between us and you, you children of Reuben and children of Gad; you have no portion in the LORD.' Thus your children would cause our children to cease fearing the LORD.
verses.22:26: Therefore we said: Let us now prepare to build an altar for ourselves, not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice,
verses.22:27: but that it may be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of the LORD before Him with our burnt offerings, with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings, so that your children will not say to our children in time to come, 'You have no portion in the LORD.'
verses.22:28: And we said: It shall be, when they say this to us or to our generations in time to come, that we will say, 'Behold the pattern of the altar of the LORD which our fathers made, not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice, for it is a witness between us and you.'
verses.22:29: Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and to turn away this day from following the LORD, by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering, or for sacrifice, apart from the altar of the LORD our God that is before His tabernacle."
verses.22:30: Now when Phinehas the priest, the chiefs of the congregation, and the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him heard the words that the children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the children of Manasseh spoke, it was pleasing in their sight.
verses.22:31: And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said to the children of Reuben, to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh, "This day we know that the LORD is in our midst, because you have not committed this treachery against the LORD; now you have delivered the children of Israel from the hand of the LORD."
verses.22:32: Then Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the chiefs, returned from the children of Reuben and the children of Gad, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and brought back word to them.
verses.22:33: And the report was pleasing in the sight of the children of Israel, and the children of Israel blessed God; and they spoke no more of going up against them in war to destroy the land in which the children of Reuben and the children of Gad dwelt.
verses.22:34: And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad named the altar, "It is a Witness between us that the LORD is God."
verses.23:1: Now it came to pass, many days after the LORD had given rest to Israel from all their enemies on every side, that Joshua was old and advanced in years.
verses.23:2: Then Joshua called all Israel, their elders, their heads, their judges, and their officers, and said to them, "I am old and advanced in years.
verses.23:3: And you have seen all that the LORD your God has done to all these nations because of you, for the LORD your God, He is the One who has fought for you.
verses.23:4: Behold, I have allotted to you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan, together with all the nations that I have cut off, as far as the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun.
verses.23:5: And the LORD your God Himself will thrust them back from before you and dispossess them from your presence, and you shall possess their land, just as the LORD your God has spoken to you.
verses.23:6: Therefore be very strong to keep and to do all that is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, not turning aside from it to the right hand or to the left,
verses.23:7: that you do not mingle with these nations, these that remain among you; and you shall not make mention of the name of their gods, nor swear by them, nor serve them, nor bow down to them.
verses.23:8: Rather, you shall cleave to the LORD your God, just as you have done to this day.
verses.23:9: For the LORD has driven out from before you great and mighty nations; and as for you, not a man has stood before you to this day.
verses.23:10: One man of you shall chase a thousand, for the LORD your God, He is the One who fights for you, just as He spoke to you.
verses.23:11: Therefore be very watchful over your souls, to love the LORD your God.
verses.23:12: For if you indeed turn back, and cleave to the remnant of these nations, these that remain among you, and intermarry with them, and go in among them and they among you,
verses.23:13: know for a certainty that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations from before you; rather, they shall become a snare and a trap to you, and a scourge on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land which the LORD your God has given you.
verses.23:14: And behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth. And you know in all your hearts and in all your souls that not one word has failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spoke concerning you; all have come to pass for you, not one word of them has failed.
verses.23:15: And it shall come to pass, that just as every good thing has come upon you which the LORD your God spoke to you, so the LORD will bring upon you every evil thing, until He has destroyed you from this good land which the LORD your God has given you.
verses.23:16: When you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD shall burn against you, and you shall perish swiftly from the good land which He has given you."
verses.24:1: Then Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem and summoned the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges, and its officers; and they presented themselves before God.
verses.24:2: And Joshua said to all the people, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'From of old your fathers dwelt beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor—and they served other gods.
verses.24:3: Then I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, led him throughout all the land of Canaan, multiplied his offspring, and gave him Isaac.
verses.24:4: To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave Mount Seir to possess it, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
verses.24:5: Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt according to what I did in its midst; and afterward I brought you out.
verses.24:6: So I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea; and the Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.
verses.24:7: When they cried out to the LORD, He placed thick darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them and covered them. Your own eyes beheld what I did in Egypt; and you dwelt in the wilderness for many days.
verses.24:8: Then I brought you into the land of the Amorites, who dwelt beyond the Jordan, and they fought against you. But I gave them into your hand, so that you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
verses.24:9: Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel, and he sent and summoned Balaam the son of Beor to curse you.
verses.24:10: But I was unwilling to listen to Balaam; instead, he assuredly blessed you, and I delivered you out of his hand.
verses.24:11: Then you crossed over the Jordan and came to Jericho. And the citizens of Jericho fought against you—the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—and I gave them into your hand.
verses.24:12: I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out from before you—the two kings of the Amorites—not by your sword nor by your bow.
verses.24:13: I have given you a land for which you did not labor, and cities which you did not build, and you dwell in them; from vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant, you eat.'
verses.24:14: Now therefore, fear the LORD and serve Him in integrity and in truth; put away the gods which your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
verses.24:15: And if it is evil in your sight to serve the LORD, choose for yourselves today whom you shall serve—whether the gods whom your fathers served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you dwell. Yet as for me and my household, we shall serve the LORD."
verses.24:16: Then the people answered and said, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD to serve other gods;
verses.24:17: for the LORD our God is He who brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, who performed these great signs before our eyes, and who preserved us along every way in which we went and among all the peoples through whose midst we passed.
verses.24:18: Moreover, the LORD drove out from before us all the peoples, including the Amorites who dwelt in the land. Therefore we also shall serve the LORD, for He is our God."
verses.24:19: But Joshua said to the people, "You are not able to serve the LORD, for He is a holy God; He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your transgression or your sins.
verses.24:20: If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, then He will turn and bring harm upon you and consume you, after He has dealt well with you."
verses.24:21: And the people said to Joshua, "No, rather we shall serve the LORD!"
verses.24:22: So Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD for yourselves, to serve Him." And they said, "We are witnesses."
verses.24:23: "Now therefore, put away the foreign gods that are in your midst, and incline your heart to the LORD, the God of Israel."
verses.24:24: And the people said to Joshua, "The LORD our God we shall serve, and His voice we shall obey."
verses.24:25: So Joshua made a covenant with the people on that day, and set for them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.
verses.24:26: Then Joshua wrote these words in the Book of the Law of God; and he took a large stone and set it up there beneath the oak that was in the sanctuary of the LORD.
verses.24:27: And Joshua said to all the people, "Behold, this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words of the LORD which He spoke with us. Therefore it shall be a witness against you, lest you deny your God."
verses.24:28: Then Joshua sent the people away, each man to his inheritance.
verses.24:29: And Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who knew all the work of the LORD which He had done for Israel.
verses.24:30: Now it came to pass after these things that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being one hundred and ten years old.
verses.24:31: And they buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath-serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north side of Mount Gaash.
verses.24:32: As for the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel had brought up from Egypt, they buried them at Shechem, in the parcel of the field which Jacob had purchased from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for one hundred pieces of silver; and it became an inheritance for the children of Joseph.
verses.24:33: And Eleazar the son of Aaron died; and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.

notes.1:4: "The Great Sea toward the going down of the sun" designates the Mediterranean Sea on the western boundary of the promised land.
notes.1:8: The Hebrew verb rendered "act wisely" (sakal) carries the combined nuance of prudent insight and the good success that flows from obeying God's law.
notes.1:14: The Hebrew term translated "armed" (chamushim) refers to troops equipped and arrayed for battle, perhaps originally organized in fivefold divisions.
notes.2:4: The Hebrew literally reads "and hid him" with a singular suffix, used distributively for hiding each of the two spies.
notes.2:13: The Ketiv (written consonants) reads a form that may be taken as singular or defective plural ("my sister" or "my sisters"), while the Qere (read tradition) explicitly reads plural "my sisters," followed here.
notes.2:18: The Hebrew word for "cord" (tiqvah) is identical in form to the word for "hope" or "expectation," lending quiet resonance to Rahab's sign of deliverance.
notes.3:11: The Hebrew literally stacks "the ark of the covenant, the Lord of all the earth," identifying the ark closely with the sovereign presence of the LORD (compare verse 13).
notes.3:15: Spring snowmelt from Mount Hermon during the barley and wheat harvest swelled the Jordan over its banks, underscoring the magnitude of the miracle.
notes.3:16: The Ketiv (written text) reads "at Adam" (be-Adam), whereas the Qere (read tradition) reads "from Adam" (me-Adam), followed here; the town lay roughly eighteen miles north of Jericho.
notes.4:6: "In time to come" translates Hebrew machar, literally "tomorrow," used idiomatically for future generations (so also in 4:21).
notes.4:18: The qere reads ka'alot ("when ... had come up"), whereas the ketiv reads ba'alot ("at the coming up of").
notes.4:23: "Red Sea" renders Hebrew Yam-Suph, literally "Sea of Reeds."
notes.5:1: The qere reads avram ("they had crossed over"), while the ketiv reads avarnu ("we had crossed over"), a first-person perspective also echoed in 5:6.
notes.5:3: "The Hill of the Foreskins" translates the Hebrew place name Gibeath-haaraloth.
notes.5:9: The place name Gilgal plays on the Hebrew verb galloti ("I have rolled away").
notes.5:14: "My lord" renders Hebrew adoni, a respectful address to a superior, though the commander's acceptance of homage and his charge in 5:15 echo the theophany at the burning bush in Exodus 3:5.
notes.6:5: The qere reads kesham'akhem ("when you hear"), whereas the ketiv reads besham'akhem ("at your hearing").
notes.6:7: The qere reads singular wayyomer ("and he said," referring to Joshua), whereas the ketiv reads plural wayyomeru ("and they said").
notes.6:9: The qere reads the construct participle toqe'ei ("who blew"), whereas the ketiv reads the perfect verb taq'u ("they blew").
notes.6:13: The qere reads the infinitive absolute halokh (indicating continuous action), whereas the ketiv reads the participle holekh ("going").
notes.6:17: "Devoted to destruction" renders Hebrew cherem, denoting things or persons irrevocably set apart to the LORD under the ban of total destruction.
notes.7:1: The Hebrew term cherem refers to persons or spoils irrevocably set apart to the LORD, either for complete destruction or for the sanctuary treasury.
notes.7:21: The qere (read form) va'ere and the ketiv (written form) both mean "and I saw," differing only in orthographic length. "Bar of gold" translates the literal Hebrew "tongue of gold."
notes.7:25: Joshua's words play on the sound of Achan's name and the Hebrew verb akar ("to bring trouble upon"), giving rise to the name Valley of Achor ("Valley of Trouble") in verse 26.
notes.8:12: In this critical text, verse 12 includes the material numbered as verse 13 in standard versification. "Rear guard" translates the literal Hebrew "its heel," referring to the ambush unit positioned behind the city.
notes.8:16: The translation follows the qere (read form) "in Ai," whereas the ketiv (written form) reads "in the city."
notes.8:20: "They had no power" renders the vivid Hebrew idiom "there were no hands in them."
notes.9:2: In the Saints Critical Text, the Mount Ebal altar and covenant renewal ceremony—placed at Joshua 8:30-35 in standard Masoretic numbering—stands here within 9:2, reflecting an ancient sequence attested in the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Septuagint.
notes.9:4: The Hebrew verb rendered "posed as envoys" derives from the root for messenger or envoy; some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions read a nearly identical verb meaning "took provisions for themselves."
notes.9:7: In the ketiv/qere variants, the qere reads singular "said" to agree with the collective Hebrew "man of Israel" (translated "the men of Israel"), whereas the ketiv reads plural "they said"; the second variant is purely orthographic between full and shortened spellings of "shall I make."
notes.10:13: The Book of Jashar—meaning "Book of the Upright"—was an ancient Israelite collection of heroic poetry and national songs, also cited in Second Samuel.
notes.10:14: Following the shorter critical textual tradition attested in the Septuagint, this text omits traditional verses fifteen and forty-three, which record an interim return to the camp at Gilgal.
notes.10:21: "Moved his tongue" renders a vivid Hebrew idiom literally meaning "sharpened his tongue," expressing that no one dared speak a single word of threat or defiance against Israel.
notes.11:2: The Hebrew naphoth denotes elevated uplands or heights along the coastal plain near Dor, and Chinneroth is the plural form of the name for the Sea of Galilee and its adjacent region.
notes.11:13: Hebrew tillam refers to the fortified mounds, or tells, formed by successive layers of settlement upon which ancient Canaanite cities stood.
notes.11:17: Hebrew ha-har he-halaq literally means 'the smooth mountain' or 'the bare mountain,' marking the southern boundary of Joshua's campaigns toward Seir.
notes.12:4: The Rephaim were an ancient people of giant stature who inhabited parts of Transjordan and Canaan prior to the Israelite conquest.
notes.12:18: Hebrew la-Sharon may be read either as the proper name Lasharon or as a geographical designation meaning 'of Sharon,' referring to the coastal plain.
notes.12:23: Hebrew goyim literally means 'nations' and here functions either as a proper name, Goiim, or as a designation for a coalition of peoples associated with Gilgal.
notes.13:4: Mearah may be a proper place name or the Hebrew common noun meaning "cave," referring to a Sidonian stronghold.
notes.13:8: The Hebrew literally reads "with him," referring to the eastern half-tribe of Manasseh who had already received their land across the Jordan.
notes.13:26: The Hebrew form rendered "of Debir" may alternatively be read as the place name Lidbir or Lo-debar.
notes.13:30: The expression "towns of Jair" translates the Hebrew Havvoth Jair, meaning the tent-villages or settlements of Jair.
notes.14:8: The Hebrew verb rendered "made ... melt" employs an unusual Aramaic-influenced spelling of the causative stem.
notes.14:12: The Hebrew phrase translated "this hill country" literally means "this mountain," referring to the highland territory around Hebron.
notes.14:15: Kiriath Arba means "City of Arba" (or "Fourfold City"), here associated with Arba, the foremost warrior among the Anakim.
notes.15:2: The Hebrew word translated "bay" literally means "tongue," referring to the southern inlet of the Salt Sea.
notes.15:4: The Masoretic Ketiv reads the singular verb "was," while the Qere reads the plural "were" to agree with the plural noun "ends"; the translation follows the Qere. The shift to the second-person plural "your" echoes the southern border description in Numbers 34:3-5.
notes.15:19: "Negev" refers to the arid southern region of Judah, which made springs of water vital for sustaining land and flocks.
notes.15:32: The summary total "twenty-nine" faithfully renders the Masoretic Text, though the preceding catalog lists more than twenty-nine individual names, some of which may be compound names or dependent settlements.
notes.15:47: The Masoretic Ketiv reads "the border," while the Qere reads "the Great" for "the Great Sea" (the Mediterranean); the translation follows the Qere.
notes.15:52: The Masoretic Text reads "Rumah," whereas some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions read "Dumah."
notes.15:53: The Masoretic Ketiv spells the town name "Janim," while the Qere reads "Janum"; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.15:63: The Masoretic Ketiv uses the imperfect form of the verb "be able," while the Qere uses the perfect form; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.16:1: The Hebrew phrase 'waters of Jericho' refers to the abundant springs near Jericho that marked the eastern starting point of the southern border of Joseph's territory.
notes.16:3: The Masoretic text spells the word for 'its farthest limits' defectively without a yod, though it conveys the same plural meaning as in verse 8.
notes.16:10: The Hebrew phrase for 'forced labor' denotes an ongoing tribute of conscripted service imposed on the Canaanite inhabitants rather than complete expulsion.
notes.17:7: Literally 'to the right hand,' which denotes southward in Hebrew geographical orientation facing the rising sun.
notes.17:11: The Hebrew term rendered 'dependent towns' is literally 'her daughters,' signifying satellite villages attached to a major city, while 'three elevated regions' translates a rare phrase referring to three upland districts.
notes.17:14: The sons of Joseph address Joshua in the collective first-person singular, speaking as a single united house to request a larger territorial allotment.
notes.18:12: The Masoretic ketiv reads the singular verb 'and it was,' while the qere reads the plural 'and they were' in grammatical agreement with 'its farthest limits'; this translation follows the qere.
notes.18:14: As in verse 12, the Masoretic ketiv has a singular verb whereas the qere reads the plural verb matching 'its farthest limits'; this translation follows the qere.
notes.18:19: The Masoretic ketiv reads a singular verb with 'its limits,' while the qere reads a plural verb with 'the limits of the boundary'; this translation follows the qere.
notes.18:24: The Masoretic ketiv reads the place name as 'Chephar Haammoni,' whereas the qere reads 'Chephar Haammonah,' rendered here as Chephar Ammonah.
notes.19:22: Shahazimah follows the traditional Hebrew reading (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) has Shahazumah.
notes.19:27: On the left reflects the Hebrew directional idiom for north when facing east.
notes.19:29: And its endpoints were follows the traditional Hebrew reading (Qere) rather than the written variant (Ketiv) of the verb.
notes.19:48: Went beyond them renders a Hebrew idiom indicating that the Danites' allotted territory slipped from them or proved insufficient, prompting their northern campaign.
notes.20:3: Unintentionally, without knowledge distinguishes accidental manslaughter from premeditated murder.
notes.20:8: Golan follows the traditional Hebrew reading (Qere); the written text (Ketiv) reads Galon.
notes.21:2: The Hebrew term rendered pasturelands denotes the open, unbuilt grazing and common lands surrounding each Levitical city for livestock, as prescribed in Numbers 35:2-5.
notes.21:27: The Hebrew Qere reads Golan, which is followed here, whereas the consonantal Ketiv spells the name with transposed letters as Galon or Golon.
notes.21:36: Verses 36 and 37 are enclosed in double brackets because they are absent from several leading Masoretic manuscripts, including the Leningrad Codex, though they are preserved in other Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint, and 1 Chronicles 6:78-79, and are required to reach the stated totals of twelve Merarite cities in verse 40 and forty-eight Levitical cities in verse 41.
notes.21:45: The phrase Not a single word failed translates the Hebrew idiom meaning literally that not a word fell to the ground, signifying the complete fulfillment of the LORD's covenant promises.
notes.22:7: The translation follows the qere (read text) be'ever ('on the side of'); the ketiv (written text) reads me'ever ('from beyond').
notes.22:14: The Hebrew term rendered 'thousands' (alphey) designates the principal tribal clans or military divisions of Israel.
notes.22:22: The solemn invocation stacks three Hebrew divine titles—El ('Mighty One'), Elohim ('God'), and YHWH ('the LORD')—and repeats them to underscore the gravity of the oath.
notes.22:34: The Masoretic Hebrew moves directly from 'named the altar' into the explanatory clause 'for it is a witness between us,' leaving the name 'Witness' (Hebrew Ed) to be understood directly from the declaration.
notes.23:4: 'I have allotted' translates Hebrew hippalti, literally 'I have caused to fall,' referring to the division of tribal territories by casting lots.
notes.23:13: 'Scourge' translates a rare Hebrew term (shotet) related to 'whip,' depicting the remaining nations as an enduring affliction upon Israel.
notes.23:14: 'The way of all the earth' is a solemn Hebrew idiom for death as the universal lot of humanity.
notes.24:3: The ketiv spells the verb in a shortened form while the qere reads the full Hiphil form meaning "and I multiplied," with no difference in sense.
notes.24:8: The ketiv appends a final he to the verb while the qere reads the standard Hiphil form meaning "and I brought."
notes.24:15: The ketiv reads "in the region beyond" while the qere reads "from beyond," matching the phrasing of verse 3.
notes.24:19: The Hebrew phrase for "a holy God" pairs a plural adjective with the plural form of the divine title Elohim to convey majesty and absolute holiness.
notes.24:32: The Hebrew term qesitah refers to an ancient unit of weight or currency of uncertain value, traditionally rendered "pieces of silver."
